note: Labels written with the KB, before any model call. supported = the cited file states or directly implies the claim. kind: supported / contradicts / silent.

claims.claim: An unarmed lane records nothing even if the swimmer touches the pad.
Two of the three backup buttons must be pressed for a backup time to count.
Times can only be pulled by the results laptop after the race is saved.
Swimmer names are loaded from a USB key, not sent over the timing cable.
The scoreboard laptop and the results laptop do not need matching COM port numbers.
If a lane fault moves with the pad when pads are swapped, the pad is faulty.
Disabling USB selective suspend helps keep the scoreboard serial adapter awake.
After a power cut the console boots with the course set to 25 yards.
The scoreboard laptop's USB serial adapter only works reliably in the left USB port.
A one-lap test race is run about an hour before the meet.
A spare 15 m scoreboard cable is kept at the timing desk.
Backup button B is blue.
Pressing Reset without Save keeps the race so it can be pulled later.
A single backup button press is enough for a backup time to count.
On this rig, live names reach the board over the RS-485 outputs.
A console that shuts down within a minute of starting usually has a faulty touch pad.
The spare horn battery is kept in the scoreboard laptop bag.
The H8-8 harness serves 10 lanes.
Two spare touch pads are kept at the timing desk.
The console's touch screen can be calibrated from the Settings menu.
BoardLink can show swimmer photos on the board.
Officials meet at the timing desk 30 minutes before the meet.
A blown fuse inside the console can be replaced on deck.
The start horn volume can be adjusted with a dial.
